newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to start rebuilding oil tanks in September.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to start rebuilding oil tanks in September.

text.p: Sri Lanka is expected to start rebuilding oil storage tanks destroyed in a Tamil Tiger rebel attack in September this year, officials at the state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) said on Tuesday.

Firms from five countries -- Japan, Korea, China, Singapore and Italy -- have tendered to rebuild the tanks destroyed during a daring raid by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) in October 1995 at the two main oil depots in Colombo, they said.

"We will put up 14 tanks altogether," said an official who declined to be identified. "With the government policy of increasing thermal power and rising demand for diesel and petrol we need to have more storage tanks," the official said.
The successful bidder will rebuild oil tanks destroyed at the Orugodawatte and Kolonnawa oil storage facilities in Colombo, he said.
The selected firm will also build a new small oil storage facility at the Sapugaskanda oil refinery, just north of the capital, he added.
The rebels, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east, damaged or destroyed up to 16 tanks in the attack.
The Asian Development Bank has given a soft loan of $24 million for the reconstruction. The CPC has to find local funding to the extent of 1.6 billion rupees, other officials said.
